summary: Node data teardown called from GameDataFileIO; structural twin of LinkedListNodeDestructor_a900 (004ba900). Reads the byte flag at this+0xC and returns it in every path. When the flag is non-zero the data block is torn down: the primary data pointer at this+0x0 is freed, and its secondary pointer at obj+0x4 is freed first if non-null. Unlike the twin, this function never frees the node buffer itself and returns the original flag value, not the node pointer.

operations.description: Read the byte flag at this+0xC into result.
Data teardown runs only when the byte flag at this+0xC is non-zero.
Load the primary data block pointer from this+0x0 into v2.
Proceed with the teardown only when the pointer at this+0x0 is non-null.
Free the secondary pointer only when the data block's dword at obj+0x4 is non-null.
Free the secondary data pointer v2[1] via FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Free the primary data block v2 via FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Return the original byte flag value (this[12]) in all paths.

unresolved: Owner class and the concrete layout of the data block (primary and secondary pointers) are unknown.
Whether obj+0x4 belongs to the same object as this is not proven; only an equal-offset reading is used.
Semantics of the flag at this+0xC beyond enabling the data teardown are unknown.
Why the node buffer itself is not freed here (unlike the twin at 004ba900) is unresolved; the caller GameDataFileIO may own it.
